newsitem.title: UK: Unilever Europe, Far East drives profits.
newsitem.headline: Unilever Europe, Far East drives profits.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch food to consumer products group Unilever Plc/NV saw the benefits in its first quarter from improved margins in Europe and a much stronger performance from its Asia Pacific region.
"If I had to highlight two particular factors it would be the margin improvement in Europe and the big increase at operating level from south east Asia," said Unilever press officer Mike Haines.
The company posted a 16 percent increase in its first quarter trading profits before exceptionals to 661 million stg after much higher than forecast exceptional charges of 76 million stg.

Profits in Europe rose 106 million to 360 million stg although sales were up just one percent margins improved 2.6 percent to 9.4 percent. Margins were helped also by a pensions benefit and the absence of a write-off of 14 million stg due to the beef crisis in the first quarter of last year.

Europe was helped especially by increased sales of personal products driven by deodorants like Lynx in Britain and perfumes after the launch of cKbe in several countries and the roll out of Elizabeth Arden Fifth Avenue outside Britain, said Haines.
The exceptionally warm weather over Easter helped ice-cream as well as deodorant sales, he said.

Unilever's Asia Pacific businesses showed a 17 million increase in trading profit to 107 million with a strong performance from Thailand and the Philippines on sales of Unilever's home and personal care products, said Haines.
Sales of detergents Viso and Haso in Vietnam grew while India put in a very strong performance and after a difficult period Australia showed good sales growth in personal care products, he added.
Unilever shares were 20p higher at 1643p in early trade after a stronger than forecast rise in underlying profits after exceptionals.

"The main reason is that the market has looked at the operating profit before exceptional items and seen that its up 16 percent and has then looked at how margins have improved in Europe," said Paribas analyst John Campbell.
